### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7939732f3520015a9201f924998632deda118ea6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f5ae5fb8f81f029b9a64b4db6adc8f5c36b3fb06` — the merge of head `0237272ee3f9eee0f4ed263f354ef3eb12dbb684` into base `7939732f3520015a9201f924998632deda118ea6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f5ae5fb8f81f029b9a64b4db6adc8f5c36b3fb06 && git checkout f5ae5fb8f81f029b9a64b4db6adc8f5c36b3fb06
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7939732f3520015a9201f924998632deda118ea6 0237272ee3f9eee0f4ed263f354ef3eb12dbb684 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7939732f3520015a9201f924998632deda118ea6 && git merge --no-ff 0237272ee3f9eee0f4ed263f354ef3eb12dbb684

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7939732f3520015a9201f924998632deda118ea6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1 review — PR #37268 at `0237272ee3f9eee0f4ed263f354ef3eb12dbb684` (2026-11-25T10:05Z)

**L1: PASS** (one-shot reviewer subagent; card #35885, `Part of #35885`)

- Shape: `l1-face.mjs --pr 37268` CLEAN at this head (13 items: draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #35885`, no closing keyword, changeset covers both touched packages, floor checks success, 37 success / 16 expected skip as the seat read). `Part of` is right: item 4 (the ADR-0158 amendment) stays with the seat, so the card must not close; `pm:dispatched` comes off by hand at landing.
- Item 1 (re-point onto a blank field): `detectDestructiveObjectChanges` (`protocol-write-face.ts`) raises `unit_mode_to_record` on the quantity when a stored record-mode quantity's `unitField` moves to a field that was no unit code field before the save and that `newlyDeclaredUnitCodeFieldsOf` does not claim. The three neighbours hold in the code as read: onto a stored text field ⇒ `declaredUnitCodeFields` has it, so `unit_code_field_declared` alone; onto a field already a unit code field ⇒ `prevUnitCodeFields` has it, nothing; the old mode-switch arm is the `else if`, so a quantity is never named twice. Reads no row. One caller only (`protocol-save.ts:1209`), which already carries `force`; no second path to miss.
- Item 1 pin is real: `protocol-destructive-unit-mode.test.ts:177` asserts `code: 'DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE'`, `status: 409`, the single issue's `code` and `field`, the wording, the remedy parts, `readNoRow`, and `force: true` ⇒ `[]`. The once-only table gains two rows (`mat_gross`, `mat_pair`) and its "named exactly once" loop now covers a re-point. The sibling pins (`:145` stored text field, `:197` code field to code field ⇒ nothing) were already on main.
- Item 2 (`unusedEntry`): set after the walk on `member` / `retired` / `other-dimension` values that are mapping keys; printed as one `⚠` line each. Pinned on the report value (`toEqual`, exact), the printed line, and the negative (no line without such an entry).
- Item 3 (capped walk): the card allowed "refused, or said plainly"; the PR says it plainly and keeps the currency twin's shape, with the unscoped-organization line word for word that of `record-currency-backfill.ts:537`. Pinned: capped apply writes the 2 examined rows, the rows past the cap are untouched, `unitCodeBackfillComplete` is false, both lines exact, and the uncapped run is refused with `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, `status: 400`.
- Changeset read sentence by sentence against the diff: all three bullets hold ("a re-point onto a stored text field still raises `unit_code_field_declared` alone" = pin `:145`; "still raises nothing" = pin `:197`; "an apply run over such a walk still writes the rows it examined, as before" = no engine change in the diff, only the report).
- No file outside the card; no generated artefact; no SQL or id materialisation added.

Findings

- N1 (nit): the re-point arm's second cause, a target that existed before the save but was not stored, has no pin of its own; only the new-field cause is pinned at `:177`. The predicate is the same `!prevUnitCodeFields.has` test either way. Follow-up at most.
- N2 (nit): in `walkUnitCodes` the `!used.has(v.value)` test can never be false for a value whose disposition is not `mapped` (values are keyed by value), so it is dead but harmless.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `0237272ee3f9eee0f4ed263f354ef3eb12dbb684`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-face.ts, packages/objectql/src/unit-code-backfill.ts + packages/objectql/src/protocol-destructive-unit-mode.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/unit-code-backfill.test.ts, .changeset/35885-unit-repoint-backfill-gaps.md
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff touches no published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`) and no governed rule text; it declares `Clause-②: no` with no arm. The record is here because the new 409 refuses a save that main accepts, which would be a narrowing if the surface were published.
- The claim "the unit surface is unreleased" holds, verified three ways. (a) At the last release tag `@objectstack/metadata-protocol@18.6.0` (npm `latest` = 18.6.0), `git grep` finds no `unit_mode_to_record`, no `unit_code_field_declared` under `packages/metadata-protocol/src` or `packages/objectql/src`, and no `unitConfig` under `packages/spec/src`. (b) On `origin/main` the surface is carried only by pending changesets: `35489-unit-config`, `35491-unit-raw-aggregate`, `35492-unit-code-backfill`, `35970-catalog-units`, `36082-record-unit-summary`. (c) No package `CHANGELOG.md` on `origin/main` mentions `unit_mode_to_record`, `unitConfig` or `migrate unit-codes`.
- So the refusal narrows nothing a released version accepts: no 18.6.0 author can write a `record`-mode `unitConfig` at all. `Clause-②: no` holds, and no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
- Noted, not a finding: npm also carries a `next` dist-tag (`0.0.0-next-…` snapshot of main). A snapshot is the pending changesets, not a release; the card itself grades this "unpublished surface until the R1 release".

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: none` with `patch` on both packages is right: no key, value or type an author can write is added or removed. The finding is a force-liftable destructive-change guard under an existing code (`unit_mode_to_record`), not a refusal of a shape; `force: true` saves the same metadata. Both packages already take `minor` from the pending `35492` changeset (`Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`), so the release level is unchanged.
- `unusedEntry` is an optional field added to a report type that is itself unreleased; additive either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Error envelope: the existing `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` / 409 with an existing issue code; no new code for a client to learn, and the pin asserts `code` and `status`.
- No row read in the detector (pinned by `readNoRow`); the backfill change is report-only, the walk and write paths are untouched. No id materialisation or in-application join added.
- PR author is the fleet bot; nothing to name.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35885-unit-repoint-backfill-gaps`
Reviewed-by: `session_011y7As5bdhV5T4N9vpjmZzH`

**VERDICT: PASS**
